{{Quote|Welcome to Qina, and blessed be the luminous mandibles of Antikra the Egglayer.|Qina spaceport public broadcast|<ref name="Tessent" />}}
'''Qina''' was a [[Temperature/Legends|cool]], lush [[Moon/Legends|moon]] that [[Orbit/Legends|orbited]] the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Hanchin]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell sector]]. It featured [[Forest/Legends|forests]], [[Mountain/Legends|mountain]] peaks, and [[Water/Legends|river]] valleys on its surface and was [[Homeworld/Legends|home]] to the creatures known as [[dochinie]], [[pech]], and [[rujo]]. Qina was inhabited by approximately two million [[Human/Legends|Humans]] as well as members of the [[Ayrou/Legends|Ayrou]] and [[Vashan]] [[Species/Legends|species]], and Qinan landholders [[Farmer/Legends|kept]] herds of the local pechs and rujos.

Each [[Local year|year]] at mid-[[Winter/Legends|winter]], the moon's population nearly doubled when Vashan pilgrims traveled there from their homeworld [[Vasha/Legends|Vasha]]. The penitents trekked on [[Limb/Legends|foot]] to the remote [[Inicus Mont]], which was a holy site in the [[Vashan religion]]. At [[Hanchin-set]], a ritual took place wherein Vashan [[Bodhi (Vashan)|bodhi]]s, who resided in Inicus Mont's [[Cave/Legends|caves]], appeared in the cave-mouths and expectorated stones known as [[sin-bullet]]s from their [[Stomach/Legends|antestomaches]]. The Vashan pilgrims would then fight over the sin-bullets, the consumption of which was believed to absolve the penitents of the prior year's misdeeds.

At some point by [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], the Vashan caste [[Theocracy|theocrat]] [[Dochi At-Rial]], who had in [[Gender/Legends|his]] possession the [[Tessent|artifact]] known as the [[Ayrou Tessent]], fled to Qina after being confronted over it by a group of [[Treasure hunting/Legends|treasure hunters]] on Vasha. The group followed At-Rial to Qina, where it retrieved the artifact and subsequently hired the bodhi [[Brixbrax Ux-rox]] to confirm the Tessent's authenticity via [[Psychometry/Legends|psychic reading]]. During the visit on Qina, the treasure [[Hunting/Legends|hunters]] also engaged in [[Space warfare/Legends|space combat]] against the [[Starship/Legends|starships]] of their rivals.

==Description==
{{Quote|It is our sincere wish that even those unable to consume a sin-bullet during this time of penitence find peace among the blissful spires of Qina.|Qina spaceport public broadcast|<ref name="Tessent" />}}
Qina<ref name="TEA" /> was a terrestrial [[Moon/Legends|moon]] that [[Orbit/Legends|orbited]] the [[Gas giant/Legends|gas giant]]&ndash;type [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Hanchin]],<ref name="Endor" /> a part of the [[Qina system/Legends|Qina system]]. It lay within the [[Inner Moddell systems]] area of<ref name="TEA" /> the [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell sector]],<ref name="EAOC Qina" /> one of the [[Sector/Legends|subsectors]] making up the [[Inner Zuma Region]]<ref name="TEA" /> within the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Zuma sector/Legends|Zuma sector]].<ref name="EAOC Qina" /> It was connected via [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]] to the [[Kuna's Tooth system/Legends|Kuna's Tooth]], [[Thonner system/Legends|Thonner]], and [[Trindello system/Legends|Trindello systems]].<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:Qina-TEA.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Qina's location in the Moddell sector]]
Qina's [[local year]] lasted three hundred [[Local day/Legends|local days]], each of which was twenty-one [[Standard hour/Legends|standard hours]] long&mdash;though the moon was washed in the eerie light of Hanchin, which rendered the natural satellite's nights short to non-existent.<ref name="Endor" /> On the rare occasions where a part of Qina's surface did not receive light from Hanchin, the resultant brief period of darkness was known by the moon's native inhabitants as a [[Hanchin-set]].<ref name="CSWE Hanchinset">{{CSWECite|II|13|Hanchin-set}}</ref> The moon was both [[Color/Legends|purplish]]-blue<ref name="Endor" /> and green in color,<ref name="Tessent" /> and it appeared very small against the backdrop of the [[Gas/Legends|gas]] giant planet's glowing green bulk. It had standard [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]], a breathable Type I [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]], and a [[Temperature/Legends|cool]] climate, with [[Winter/Legends|winter]] being one of the moon's seasons<ref name="Endor" /> and a Hanchin-set regularly occurring at mid-winter.<ref name="CSWE Hanchinset" />

A wild and rugged yet beautiful world, Qina had [[Forest/Legends|forests]], jagged [[Mountain/Legends|mountain]] peaks, and steep-walled valleys through which tumbled [[Water/Legends|rivers]] and which were overflowing with lush [[Plant/Legends|vegetation]], including [[Fruit/Legends|fruit]]. Qina's [[Homeworld/Legends|native]] fauna included the<ref name="Endor" /> [[Diet/Legends|predators]]<ref name="Tessent" /> known as [[pech]]s and the eight-[[Limb/Legends|legged]], feathered, predatory gliding creatures known as [[dochinie]]s. In addition, the moon was home to a surefooted variety of the [[rujo]], a docile quadruped from the Moddell sector's [[Capital/Legends|capital]] planet [[Annaj/Legends|Annaj]].<ref name="Endor" />

==History==
{{RPG|"[[Race for the Tessent]]"}}
At some point by [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="3 ABY">By default, the events of {{GamerCite|9|Race for the Tessent}} are set during the opposition to [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] [[Slavery/Legends|slavery]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]]. ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' dates the events of [[Star Wars (1977) 69|''Star Wars'' (1977) 69]], which depict the [[Battle of the City of Bone|end]] of the Imperial presence on Mandalore per {{InsiderCite|80|The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors}}, to [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]].</ref> in [[The Abyss (Vasha)|The Abyss]] [[Mining/Legends|mine]] on the planet [[Vasha/Legends|Vasha]], [[Vashan]] [[Miner/Legends|miners]] discovered the [[Ayrou Tessent]], a [[Chalcedony/Legends|chalcedony]] idol that was one of the [[Alsakan Tessent|two]] [[Tessent]] artifacts and which, according to a legend, held encoded coordinates for a treasure vault the [[Ur-Chapterhouse]] of the ''[[il Madri]]'' religious tradition of the [[Ayrou/Legends|Ayrou]] [[Species/Legends|species]] had hidden in one of the [[Kuna systems]]. Eventually, a group of [[Treasure hunting/Legends|treasure hunters]] visited The Abyss and confronted both [[Dochi At-Rial]], a Vashan caste theocrat who had the Tessent in [[Gender/Legends|his]] possession, and the Vashan [[Sword/Legends|swordsman]] [[Poina Tuc-shol]]&mdash;who, due to religious reasons, was wary of any non-Vashans obtaining the Tessent. The former, however, managed to flee with the Tessent for the Vashan holy site of [[Inicus Mont]] on Qina, in the process discarding the [[Necklace/Legends|necklace]] of shrunken Ayrou heads that helped off-worlders distinguish the theocrat from other Vashans.<ref name="Tessent" />

[[File:QinaCombat-Gamer9.jpg|thumb|right|300px|A pair of starfighters, including a Z-95 Headhunter (right), in combat over Qina]]
The treasure [[Hunting/Legends|hunters]] pursued At-Rial to Qina, which at the [[Time/Legends|time]] was experiencing one of its regular seasons of Vashan pilgrimages to Inicus Mont, and were in turn tailed by Tuc-shol. The group then retrieved the Tessent from the Vashan theocrat, who had taken up refuge in Inicus Mont's [[Cave of the Sanctuary]], and visited the [[Cave of Memory]]. There the treasure hunters hired the Vashan [[Bodhi (Vashan)|bodhi]] [[Brixbrax Ux-rox]] to perform a [[Psychometry/Legends|psychic reading]] on the Tessent in order to confirm the artifact's authenticity. The group's rivals in the hunt for the Tessents also arrived in the [[Cave/Legends|cave]] at that time, leading to a tense situation. At some point during the treasure hunters' visit on Qina, the local guide [[Groex Gal]] lent the quartet of [[Z-95 Headhunter/Legends|Z-95 Headhunter]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] he maintained on the moon to the service of the group's cause, and the fighters eventually saw use in [[Space warfare/Legends|combat]] against the [[Starship/Legends|starships]] of the rival treasure hunters.<ref name="Tessent" />
{{Endgame}}

==Inhabitants==
{{Quote|You must make the worthy pilgrimage to the summit if you hope to catch a polished sin-bullet as it flies from a bodhi's holy mouthparts.|Qina spaceport public broadcast|<ref name="Tessent" />}}
Qina was home to a population of approximately two million [[Human/Legends|Humans]] as well as members of the Ayrou and Vashan species. Qinans governed themselves through a [[Democracy/Legends|democracy]], and they had access to [[Realspace/Legends|space]]-[[Technology level|level]] technology. Landholders on Qina [[Farmer/Legends|kept]] herds of the local pechs and rujos, and the Qinans exported fruit as well as meat and [[Leather/Legends|hides]] obtained from pechs and rujos. In return, [[Foodstuff/Legends|foodstuffs]] and technology was imported on Qina from off-world. By the time of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], addiction to the [[Rokna Blue]] [[Spice/Legends|drug]], which was also brought onto Qina from elsewhere, had become a growing problem among the moon's inhabitants.<ref name="Endor" />

[[File:Vashan2.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Vashan penitents (the Vashans Dochi At-Rial and Poina Tuc-shol pictured) visited Qina on annual pilgrimages.]]
Each year at mid-winter, the moon was visited by around two million Vashan pilgrims, which consisted of members of all Vashan [[Theocracy|theocratic]] castes.<ref name="Endor" /> The penitents were [[Transport/Legends|transported]] by the thousands from their homeworld Vasha aboard [[Freighter/Legends|freighters]] that landed on Qina every hour, only taking the time to unload the passengers and [[Fuel/Legends|refuel]] before taking off for Vasha again.<ref name="Tessent" /> The pilgrims would subsequently gather below the caves of the holy site known as Inicus Mont.<ref name="Endor" />

During Hanchin-set, the Vashan bodhis residing there appeared in the cave-mouths and expectorated the stones known as [[sin-bullet]]s from their [[Stomach/Legends|antestomaches]]. The Vashan pilgrims would then fight over the sin-bullets, with any penitent who managed to obtain one immediately consuming it and crushing it in their true stomach&mdash;a ritual that was believed to absolve the Vashan of the prior year's misdeeds. Qinans viewed the religious ceremony as slightly unusual yet still profited from it: Ayrou and Human [[Merchant/Legends|traders]] attended the crowds of pilgrims in order to sell them sustenance, rent [[Sleeper (furniture)|beds]], and provide other necessities in exchange for remuneration.<ref name="Endor" />

More than a [[Standard decade/Legends|decade]] prior to<ref name="Tessent" /> 3 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|ABY]],<ref name="3 ABY" /> the [[Ebranite]] [[Scout/Legends|scout]] and mountaineer Groex Gal came to reside on Qina, intending to establish an Ebranite [[Colonist/Legends|colony]] there. Although that endeavour failed, Gal remained on the moon, working as a scout and an unofficial tour guide for the Vashan pilgrims and over the years becoming well-known and trusted among many of them. Gal loved his work, and when the Vashan pilgrims were not visiting Qina he was willing to journey into Qina's mountains for the price of his expenses alone.<ref name="Tessent" /> Gal kept working as a tour guide on Qina into the early [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the existence of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]],<ref name="CSWE GroexGal">{{CSWECite|I|308|Gal, Groex}}</ref> which was [[Declaration of a New Republic/Legends|formed]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref>

==Locations==
{{Quote|The limestone peak of Inicus Mont contains forty-two caves in which the most perfect of the Vashan bodhis have spent the past year in prayer.|Qina spaceport public broadcast|<ref name="Tessent" />}}
Qina housed a single [[Standard Class starport|standard-class spaceport]]<ref name="Endor" /> known as [[Qina spaceport]]. During the time of the Vashan pilgrimages, it broadcast a public service announcement to all starships arriving on Qina. In the announcement, which described Qina's spires as "blissful," a brief description and coordinates were provided for four of the most-visited caves of Inicus Mont.<ref name="Tessent" /> Docking fees at the facility soared every mid-winter due to the heavy influx of pilgrims.<ref name="Endor" />

The pillar-shaped<ref name="CSWE InicusMont">{{CSWECite|II|103|Inicus Mont}}</ref> [[Limestone/Legends|limestone]] spire known as Inicus Mont, which was a holy site<ref name="Endor" /> in the [[Vashan religion|religion]] of the Vashan species,<ref name="Tessent" /> was situated in a remote corner of Qina's landmass.<ref name="CSWE InicusMont" /> The way from the Qina [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] to Inicus Mont was exhausting and treacherous, winding both through valleys with [[Tree/Legends|tree]]-covered crags, amid which wild pechs preyed upon any [[Mammal/Legends|mammalian]] travelers among the Vashan pilgrims, and across rushing rivers where the loss of footing could lead an individual to be swept over a waterfall. Despite the perils of the journey, the route intentionally did not make use of such modern conveniences as a [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] [[Air taxi/Legends|taxi]] system&mdash;and not even simple bridges across the rivers&mdash;since the Vashans found attempts to make the trip easier that way to be insulting to their religion and were known to attack anyone using a starship to travel directly to Inicus Mont.<ref name="Tessent" />

Inicus Mont was riddled with tunnels as well as<ref name="CSWE InicusMont" /> forty-two caves,<ref name="Tessent" /> inside the latter of which Vashan bodhis prayed and [[Meditation/Legends|meditated]], creating in their antestomaches polished stones known as sin-bullets as part of the [[prayer-drone]] process.<ref name="Endor" /> The swords of ancient Vashan heroes were preserved in the [[Cave of the Blade]], and, according to legend, the most venerated artifacts of Vashan religio-[[Archaeology/Legends|archaeology]] were kept in the [[Cave of the Image]]. In addition, the tour guide Groex Gal worked from a small cave enclosure on the eastern slope of the foothills of Inicus Mont. The Ebranite maintained a quartet of refitted Z-95 Headhunter starfighters&mdash;originally envisioned as a defense force for an Ebranite colony on Qina&mdash;in a hidden cave near his enclosure.<ref name="Tessent" />

==Behind the scenes==
====Race for the Tessent====
Qina first appeared in the [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] adventure "[[Race for the Tessent]]," which was published for use with [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' in the [[Star Wars Gamer 9|ninth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Gamer]]'' magazine<ref name="Tessent" /> on [[February 22]], [[2002]].<ref name="GamerDate">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/other/rpg/news20020222.html|text=Starfighters Soar in Gamer #9}}</ref> Within the magazine, it was also described in the ''Star Wars Roleplaying Game'' source article "[[Endor and the Moddell Sector]]." In that article, the moon was consistently referred to as "Mina"<ref name="Endor" />&mdash;a spelling that carried over to several entries in [[2008]]'s ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''.<ref name="CSWE Hanchinset" /><ref name="CSWE GroexGal" /><ref name="CSWE InicusMont" /><ref name="CSWE Mina">{{CSWECite|II|315|Mina}}</ref><ref name="CSWE sinbullets">{{CSWECite|III|152|sin-bullets}}</ref> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' once again used the spelling "Qina,"<ref name="TEA" /> with [[Jason Fry]], co-author of both that book<ref name="Blogspot">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2009/08/endnotes-for-star-wars-essential-atlas_31.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: The Essential Atlas (part 5 of 5)|quote=Most of this section is a rewrite of the ''Star Wars Gamer'' feature written by myself, Dan and Craig Carey. Note that Qina was misidentified as Mina in the original article.}}</ref> and the ''Star Wars Gamer'' 9 articles,<ref name="Endor" /><ref name="Tessent" /> confirming it as the correct variant of the moon's name.<ref name="Blogspot" /> ''The Essential Atlas'' placed Qina in grid square H-16.<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:Race_for_the_Tessent_G9.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Qina was introduced as a potential conclusion setting for the roleplaying adventure "Race for the Tessent."]]
Instead of featuring a set plot, "Race for the Tessent" presents several settings in the Moddell sector that the player characters may visit during their search for one of the two artifacts known as the Tessents. For each of the settings, the adventure also suggests possible circumstances for a Tessent being hidden there. This article assumes that as much of the non-contradictory information presented in the adventure as possible is [[canon]]ical with respect to the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity. Therefore, it is assumed that the Ayrou Tessent was hidden on Vasha and that the player characters visit The Abyss, where they confront both Dochi At-Rial and Poina Tuc-shol. At-Rial is assumed to have then fled to Qina with the Tessent.<ref name="Tessent" />

"Race for the Tessent" suggests that, if the player characters attempt to confront At-Rial anywhere else but in The Abyss, the theocrat immediately escapes to Qina with the Tessent. Alternately, if the player characters don't visit Vasha at all, they can still be drawn to Qina by rumors that Vashan miners have uncovered the idol and [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttled]] it to the moon for safekeeping it at Inicus Mont's Cave of the Image. The adventure also suggests that, if he is not actively pursuing the player characters, Tuc-shol may be lurking near the Cave of the Blade on Qina while waiting for any disturbance to arise at Inicus Mont.<ref name="Tessent" />

====Cave of Memory ending====
"Race for the Tessent" presents Qina's Cave of Memory as a possible site for an ending to the adventure. The adventure suggests that, while Brixbrax Ux-rox is reading psychic energies off a Tessent offered to him, the player characters' rivals in the hunt for the artifacts also arrive in the cave. It is left up to the gamemaster player's discretion to choose how Ux-rox reacts to the subsequent tense situation&mdash;the bodhi can keep the artifact in his antestomach where he is storing it during the reading; or he can either spit out the Tessent at the feet of whomever gave it to him or even expectorate the artifact out of the cave entirely and down into the amassed crowd of Vashan pilgrims.<ref name="Tessent" />

[[File:Tessent2-Gamer9.png|thumb|left|300px|The Ayrou Tessent, one of the two Tessents which may figure on Qina as part of the events of "Race for the Tessent."]]
In the case where Ux-rox proceeds to pronounce the result of his reading of the Tessent, the actions of the player characters' rival treasure hunters depend on which of the two idols has been thus identified. The [[Xenoarchaeology/Legends|xenoarchaeologist]] [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Follnor Callat]] is only interested in acquiring the Alsakan Tessent, being willing to do anything in his power to obtain it, and does not care at all about the Ayrou Tessent. The opposite is true for Tuc-shol, while the criminals known as the [[Kintan Gunrunners]] and the gang of the [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] [[Korraj]] both are only interested in the profit to be gained from selling the artifacts and are thus prepared to fight to obtain either of them.<ref name="Tessent" />

In addition, if At-Rial sees an opportunity to steal either of the two Tessents during the fighting over them, he will do so and attempt to escape into the masses of Vashan pilgrims below the Cave of Memory. Finally, Ux-rox may also proclaim either of the Tessents to be a fake, in which case one of the individuals involved in the treasure hunt can slip away unnoticed with the real artifact. This article refrains from assuming any of the abovementioned details concerning the visit to the Cave of Memory are canonical; similarly, while the space combat involving Groex Gal's starfighters is indeed assumed to have occurred at Qina, the article does not assume the specific identities of the parties involved in the confrontation.<ref name="Tessent" />
